jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Corporate Engineering
jobs.description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About The Role

As a Technical Program Manager for Corporate Engineering, you will lead programs that build world-class business solutions enabling every Ant to do their best work. In partnership with Anthropic's IT & Security organization, you will drive end-to-end solutions across the company, delivering the right products, tools, platforms, and experiences for all Ants as they work to create a world for safe and powerful AI. In the simplest terms, you build and drive solutions to enable all of Anthropic to be more productive.

You will use your technical and program management expertise to lead complex, multi-disciplinary programs from start to finish. You will work with stakeholders to plan requirements, identify risks, lead execution, and communicate clearly with cross-functional partners across the company. You are equally comfortable explaining your team's analyses and recommendations to leadership as you are discussing the technical tradeoffs in product development with engineers.

This role owns the full spectrum of Corporate Engineering programs: the IT systems Ants depend on daily, first-party and third-party software platforms, endpoint devices, office infrastructure, AV and collaboration equipment, network infrastructure, and the programs that scale our physical office footprint as Anthropic grows.

Responsibilities

Partner across Corporate Engineering domains to drive alignment and delivery: Work with globally distributed product, engineering, and architecture teams to foster collaboration, help teams adopt enterprise standards, and enable faster delivery with consistent practices across the organization
Define and maintain core architectural foundations: Assist in establishing and maintaining the architectural standards that underpin Corporate Engineering systems, ensuring scalability, reliability, and security as Anthropic grows
Lead office deployment and scaling programs: Own end-to-end planning and execution for new office buildouts and expansions, coordinating across IT, Facilities, Security, and external vendors to deliver fully operational workspaces on schedule
Own internal systems and infrastructure programs: Drive programs for all internal systems and hardware deployed in Anthropic buildings, including network infrastructure, AV equipment, printing and collaboration hardware, and building technology integrations
Lead endpoint and device management programs: Own global programs for corporate laptops, mobile devices, and endpoint management, ensuring Ants have secure, well-managed devices that enable productivity from day one
Drive IT Operations excellence: Lead programs that improve IT service delivery, support operations, and the overall Ant experience with technology, driving continuous improvement in reliability and responsiveness
Manage enterprise software and platform programs: Lead programs for the 1P and 3P software platforms Ants depend on, including HR systems, productivity tools, and business applications, from evaluation through deployment and ongoing optimization
Collaborate with cross-functional stakeholders: Work closely with Security, Facilities, People, Finance, and functional teams across Anthropic to ensure Corporate Engineering programs meet diverse organizational needs
Communicate effectively at all levels: Comfortable communicating across all levels of Anthropic from presenting analyses, recommendations, and program status to leadership, engaging deeply on technical tradeoffs with engineering teams, and communicating broadly to the entire company

You May Be a Good Fit If You Have

8+ years of experience in IT, Corporate Engineering, or Enterprise Technology, with at least 4+ years leading complex, cross-functional programs
Technical background in enterprise IT systems, including endpoint management, identity and access management, network infrastructure, and SaaS platforms
Experience leading office buildout or infrastructure deployment programs, coordinating across IT, Facilities, and external vendors
Proven experience as a Technical Program Manager or similar role in a technology-focused environment, with a track record of leading company-wide programs to successful completion
Strong communication skills with the ability to translate technical concepts for executive audiences and engage credibly with engineers on technical details
Ability to manage ambiguity and drive clarity in fast-paced, evolving environments where requirements and priorities shift
Strong collaboration skills with proven ability to partner across diverse stakeholders including IT, Security, Facilities, People, Finance, and functional teams

Strong Candidates May Also Have

Experience scaling IT infrastructure in high-growth technology companies
Background in IT service management (ITSM) frameworks and continuous improvement methodologies
Experience with enterprise software evaluation, procurement, and vendor management
Familiarity with modern endpoint management platforms and zero-trust security architectures
Experience with AV systems, video conferencing infrastructure, and collaboration technology deployments
Prior technical experience as an IT engineer, systems administrator, or network engineer
Experience with IT programs in AI/ML research environments or organizations with unique security and compliance requirements

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary

$290,000—$365,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education:
Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study:
A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience:
Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy:
Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How We're Different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Job Summary:
Performs trust accounting functions for defined benefit plans, non-qualified plans, and individual wealth management asset allocation accounts for which Pentegra Trust Company (“PTC”) provides trust and custody services. Provides benefit payment administrative services for PTC defined benefit pension plans.

Essential Functions

Work directly with pension plan clients and pensioners to resolve benefit payment matters, including tax withholding changes, banking information updates, address changes, and pension verification requests.
Maintain pensioner information on the BNY Mellon Workbench system to include generating periodic pension reports for clients.
Regular contact with Pentegra’s Benefit Payment Unit (“BPU”) regarding new pensioners and payment issues for existing clients, and with BNY Mellon regarding payment, balancing, and NEXEN issues.
Balance monthly pension payments and lump sum distributions to determine cash liquidity requirements.
Prepare quarterly trust fee billing information and submit it to the Finance Department for inclusion in semi-annual invoices.
Process invoices payable from plan assets and coordinate the related transfer of funds to the Finance Department.
Review and approve the weekly OFAC report for accounts maintained on the trust accounting system.
Process Federal tax deposits on a timely basis for the PTC IRA accounts to include reconciling the annual Form 945 filed with the IRS.
Prepare PTC settlement wires, checks and internal transfers between PTC bank clearing accounts.
Assist Trust Manager in reconciliation, preparation, and mailing of annual 1099 tax forms for PTC accounts.
Complete the daily PTC cash and custody reconciliations.
Regular contact with third-party service providers for PTC trading and banking issues.
Ensure the timely and accurate pricing of securities held in custody by PTC.
Post income and dividends for securities held in custody by PTC.
Transmit PTC mutual fund trades through the Matrix trading bridge and money market trades through the Federated trading bridge; place equity trades directly with PTCs institutional securities broker.
Oversee settlement of all PTC mutual fund trades with Matrix and other securities trades with Fifth-Third Bank as PTC’s sub-custodian.
Release settlement wire, check, and internal transfers between PTC bank clearing accounts.
Review and follow up on cash and mutual fund discrepancies from daily reconciliation of the PTC clearing and custody accounts.
Coordinate processing and voting of proxies to include plans for which PTC is the trustee for employer stock funds.
Generate the daily extract files for the wealth management asset allocation accounts, and after reviewing the extract files for accuracy, upload the files to Envestnet.
Process and post PTC contribution, distribution and trade activity on the trust accounting system.
Review, collate and mail monthly PTC statements.
As needed, cross-train on and perform other trust accounting functions to provide coverage when other Trust Operations team members are unavailable.
Assist management in implementing department goals and objectives.
Perform additional duties, responsibilities, and job functions as assigned or as business needs require.

Experience working in a trust department, in banking or familiarity with retirement plans a plus.
Proficient in Microsoft Office suite.

Team player with the ability to work independently.
Excellent communication skills.
Attention to detail with ability to multi-task.
Excellent follow-up skills.
Ability to prioritize workflow and meet daily department deadlines.
Self-motivated.

Explore this opportunity and be part of the next chapter in our history.

Mount Sinai Health System is one of the largest academic medical systems in the New York metro area, with more than 48,000 employees working across eight hospitals, more than 400 outpatient practices, more than 300 labs, a school of nursing, and a leading school of medicine and graduate education. Mount Sinai advances health for all people, everywhere, by taking on the most complex health care challenges of our time — discovering and applying new scientific learning and knowledge; developing safer, more effective treatments; educating the next generation of medical leaders and innovators; and supporting local communities by delivering high-quality care to all who need it. Through the integration of its hospitals, labs, and schools, Mount Sinai offers comprehensive health care solutions from birth through geriatrics, leveraging innovative approaches such as artificial intelligence and informatics while keeping patients’ medical and emotional needs at the center of all treatment. The Health System includes more than 9,000 primary and specialty care physicians; 13 joint-venture outpatient surgery centers throughout the five boroughs of New York City, Westchester, Long Island, and Florida; and more than 30 affiliated community health centers. We are consistently ranked by U.S. News & World Report's Best Hospitals, receiving high "Honor Roll" status, and are highly ranked: No. 1 in Geriatrics, top 5 in Cardiology/Heart Surgery, and top 20 in Diabetes/Endocrinology, Gastroenterology/GI Surgery, Neurology/Neurosurgery, Orthopedics, Pulmonology/Lung Surgery, Rehabilitation, and Urology. New York Eye and Ear Infirmary of Mount Sinai is ranked No. 12 in Ophthalmology. U.S. News & World Report’s “Best Children’s Hospitals” ranks Mount Sinai Kravis Children's Hospital among the country’s best in several pediatric specialties. The Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai is ranked No. 11 nationwide in National Institutes of Health funding and in the 99th percentile in research dollars per investigator according to the Association of American Medical Colleges. Newsweek’s “The World’s Best Smart Hospitals” ranks The Mount Sinai Hospital as No. 1 in New York and in the top five globally, and Mount Sinai Morningside in the top 20 globally.

Equal Opportunity Employer

We do not discriminate, exclude, or treat individuals differently based on race, color, national origin, age, religion, disability, sex, sexual orientation, gender, veteran status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We are deeply committed to fostering an environment where all faculty, staff, students, trainees, patients, visitors, and the communities we serve feel respected and supported. Our goal is to create a healthcare and learning institution that actively works to remove barriers, address challenges, and promote fairness in all aspects of our organization.

About The Company

Guidehouse is a leading management, technology, and risk consulting firm dedicated to helping organizations navigate complex challenges and achieve their strategic objectives. With a focus on innovation and excellence, Guidehouse serves a diverse range of clients across the public and private sectors, including federal agencies, state and local governments, and commercial enterprises. The company's commitment to integrity, diversity, and inclusion fosters a collaborative environment where talented professionals can thrive and make a meaningful impact. As a trusted partner in transformation, Guidehouse leverages deep industry expertise and cutting-edge technology to deliver tailored solutions that drive efficiency, resilience, and growth.

About The Role

The Senior Business Analyst supporting the federal Chief Information Officer (CIO) plays a vital role in enhancing office operations and project delivery across a broad spectrum of technology initiatives. This position requires a strategic thinker with extensive experience in managing complex projects, building trusted stakeholder relationships, and translating technical needs into actionable business insights. The successful candidate will lead the development of strategic plans, roadmaps, and project plans, ensuring alignment with organizational goals. They will serve as a key liaison between technical teams, agency leadership, vendors, and external stakeholders, facilitating effective communication and coordination to ensure successful project outcomes. The role involves supporting the execution of key initiatives, managing risks, and providing comprehensive briefings to executive leadership. This position offers an exciting opportunity to contribute to impactful federal technology projects and support mission-critical operations.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate must be a U.S. citizen and able to obtain and maintain a Federal or DoD "Public Trust" clearance. A minimum of eight (8) years of experience supporting technology projects is required, demonstrating a proven track record of delivering complex initiatives. Certification as a Project Management Professional (PMP) is highly preferred, with the ability to obtain certification if not already held. Candidates should possess strong experience in managing or supporting technical projects, escalating risks, and supporting enterprise systems and deployments such as IT Service Management, Change Requests, and Business Analysis. Excellent communication skills, both verbal and written, are essential for effectively engaging with stakeholders at all levels. The ability to understand complex system needs and translate them into clear business analysis is critical. A bachelor's degree is highly preferred, along with experience in federal government consulting and an active Top Secret security clearance.

Responsibilities

Support the federal CIO by enhancing office operations and project delivery across various initiatives and systems.
Lead the development of strategic plans, roadmaps, and project plans supporting complex technology integration efforts.
Provide strategic insights to clients to establish project priorities, resource allocation, and timelines while building trusted relationships with stakeholders.
Initiate, execute, and close projects of varying scope and complexity, serving as a senior business analyst.
Gather, analyze, and evaluate customer requirements across multiple systems and stakeholder groups.
Track project progress and key initiatives, ensuring success through diligent analysis and coordination.
Identify and escalate project risks and dependencies using technical expertise.
Collaborate with agency leaders, vendors, and contracting teams to support successful project delivery.
Manage and monitor data calls from internal and external stakeholders.
Create briefings and reports for client leadership to facilitate informed decision-making.
Own and execute additional initiatives as directed by the CIO, contributing to organizational goals.

Benefits

Guidehouse offers a comprehensive total rewards package designed to support the well-being and professional growth of its employees. Benefits include competitive medical, dental, and vision insurance plans, along with Rx coverage. Employees enjoy personal and family sick leave, company-paid holidays, and the potential for discretionary incentive bonuses. The firm provides parental leave and adoption assistance to support work-life balance. Retirement planning is facilitated through a 401(k) plan, complemented by life insurance options, health savings accounts, flexible spending accounts, and disability coverage. Additional perks include student loan repayment programs, tuition reimbursement, and opportunities for personal development and certifications. Guidehouse promotes a collaborative and inclusive workplace through community outreach events, employee referral programs, and emergency childcare support, fostering a supportive environment for all employees.

Equal Opportunity

Guidehouse is an Equal Opportunity Employer that values diversity and inclusion. We are committed to creating an equitable workplace where all individuals are treated with respect and fairness. Protected veterans, individuals with disabilities, and applicants from all backgrounds are encouraged to apply. Guidehouse adheres to all applicable laws and regulations regarding equal employment opportunities and will consider qualified applicants with criminal histories in accordance with relevant statutes. We ensure that our recruitment processes are free from discrimination and bias, and we provide accommodations for candidates with disabilities throughout the hiring process. Our commitment to diversity extends beyond compliance, fostering a culture of belonging and opportunity for everyone.

Job Description

The Commonwealth Cyber Initiative (CCI) is a state-funded initiative that brings together more than 40 colleges and universities, industry partners, and other stakeholders to strengthen Virginia’s cybersecurity research, education, workforce development, and innovation ecosystem. Organized through a CCI hub and four regional nodes spanning the Commonwealth, CCI supports collaboration across higher education and industry and develops programs and partnerships that help prepare Virginia’s students and workforce for the evolving cybersecurity and technology economy.

CCI is seeking a collaborative and execution-focused Program Manager to advance CCI’s workforce development mission. Based in CCI’s Arlington, VA operations, the Program Manager will design, develop, and execute workforce development initiatives that connect students with employers through experiential learning, internships, project-based learning, career preparation, and other work-based learning opportunities. The Program Manager will also partner with CCI Nodes and engage with workforce development initiatives throughout the CCI network. Reporting to the Director of Outreach, this role will strengthen industry and government partnerships, support strategic workforce initiatives, and ensure the successful delivery of programs that prepare CCI students for careers in cybersecurity and related technical fields.

The Program Manager will bring demonstrated knowledge and experience in workforce development principles, practices, and program design, with particular expertise in developing experiential learning, internship, project-based learning, and other work-based learning programs that connect students with employers and create pathways to employment.

The Program Manager will lead program execution across a portfolio of projects ranging from simple to intermediate complexity. Responsibilities include managing timelines, budgets, deliverables, and cross-functional coordination to ensure effective and timely outcomes. The role will track engagement and performance metrics, monitor progress against goals, and prepare updates and reports for leadership and key stakeholders, supporting continuous improvement and accountability.

The Program Manager will lead and support program development activities by designing and advancing workforce development initiatives in collaboration with internal leadership and external partners. This includes developing programs based on student needs, employer demand, labor-market trends, and emerging workforce needs; shaping engagement strategies; supporting experiential and applied programming; and translating strategic goals into actionable programs that respond to employer, government, student, and community needs.

In support of employer and business development, the Program Manager will cultivate and maintain relationships with public- and private-sector partners, serving as a primary point of contact to facilitate collaboration and communication. The role will identify, recruit, and steward employers who can provide internships, project-based learning opportunities, mentorship, industry projects, and employment opportunities for CCI students. The Program Manager will support partner outreach, CCI node outreach, and marketing efforts, and assist in identifying and pursuing opportunities that expand participation in and visibility of CCI’s workforce development programs.

The role will develop and maintain systems for measuring student, employer, and program outcomes and use those results to improve CCI’s workforce development initiatives.

This position is located at the Virginia Tech Research Center in Arlington, VA and is eligible for a hybrid work arrangement within a commutable distance to support a weekly in-office presence. Occasional travel may be required to support collaborative initiatives and stakeholder engagement.

Required Qualifications

Master’s degree with experience in workforce development, program management, education, business, public administration, or a related field; or Bachelor’s degree with demonstrated professional experience in workforce development, program management, or a related field in lieu of the advanced degree.
Demonstrated knowledge of and experience with workforce development principles, practices, and program design, including employer engagement, career pathways, experiential learning, internships, project-based learning, work-based learning, and strategies for connecting students or job seekers with employment opportunities.
Experience designing, implementing, or managing workforce development programs that connect students or job seekers with employers and demonstrate measurable internship, employment, or career outcomes.
Experience developing and managing relationships with employers, industry partners, program stakeholders, government agencies, educational institutions, or other workforce stakeholders to create meaningful learning and career opportunities.
Demonstrated ability to manage programs and projects from planning through implementation and completion, including managing timelines, deliverables, budgets, stakeholders, and multiple priorities.
Knowledge of labor-market and industry trends and the ability to identify workforce needs and translate those needs into program strategies and recommendations.
Ability to communicate effectively orally and in writing and to develop clear, professional communications and presentations for diverse audiences.
Strong interpersonal skills and ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with a diverse set of constituent groups, including students, program stakeholders, corporate partners, government agencies, university administrators, faculty, community colleges, and community organizations.
Ability to analyze data, including workforce, labor-market, program participation, employer engagement, and employment outcome data, and use findings to establish priorities and inform program development and continuous improvement.
Evidence of being a self-starter who can work independently while also serving effectively as a team contributor in a complex and fast-paced organization.
Demonstrated ability to set and manage multiple priorities, tasks, and deadlines simultaneously.
Experience planning and/or supporting the planning of meetings, events, workshops, or other stakeholder engagement activities.
Proficiency with office suite tools such as word processing, spreadsheets, and presentations.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience and/or education in cybersecurity, information technology, engineering, data science, or another cyber-related or technical field.
Experience developing or managing internships, apprenticeships, project-based learning, employer-sponsored projects, mentorship programs, or other work-based learning initiatives.
Experience developing and implementing career-readiness programs or career pathways that prepare students for employment in technical or high-demand fields.
Demonstrated experience establishing employer partnerships that result in internships, experiential learning opportunities, projects, mentorship, interviews, or employment for students or job seekers.

Experience working across government, industry, academia, economic development organizations, and/or venture capital.
Demonstrated networking skills, including experience developing strategic partnerships and negotiating business-to-business agreements or contracts.
Experience establishing and developing new business relationships and securing external funding or sponsorships for workforce or education programs.
Experience with grant management, proposal development, or other public- or private-sector funding mechanisms.

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
Job Title: Project Manager
Job Description

The Project Manager leads the day-to-day management of federal and commercial construction projects, ensuring they are delivered safely, on time, within budget, and in alignment with organizational goals. This role is responsible for developing comprehensive project plans that define tasks, timelines, resources, and milestones, while directing a multidisciplinary team to successfully complete projects. The Project Manager oversees budgeting, subcontractor engagement, schedule management, and risk mitigation, and serves as a key liaison between leadership, project stakeholders, and field teams throughout the life of each project.

Responsibilities

Lead all activities related to contract administration, including managing change orders, procurement, schedules, owner billing, subcontractor and vendor billing, and financial reporting.
Maintain thorough knowledge of contract terms and a clear understanding of all parties involved in each project.
Create long- and short-term project plans, set targets for milestones, and ensure adherence to established deadlines.
Delegate tasks to team members best positioned to complete them effectively and efficiently.
Make timely and effective decisions when presented with multiple options for progressing the project.
Serve as a primary point of contact for teams when multiple team members are assigned to the same project, ensuring coordinated and synergistic actions.
Communicate regularly with leadership to keep projects aligned with organizational goals and priorities.
Establish expectations and follow up with project team members to ensure quality control throughout project development and maintain expected standards.
Adjust project schedules and targets as needs, conditions, or financing requirements change.
Secure required permits and verify insurance coverage for all subcontractors involved in the project.
Facilitate project meetings to successfully coordinate work activities among internal teams and external partners.
Lead, train, and develop project team members, including Assistant Project Managers and other staff.
Prepare and submit monthly job status reports that outline project priorities, progress, and issues.
Lead project close-out activities, including turnover of manuals and warranties and preparation of final payment documents for subcontractors.
Develop and maintain positive working relationships with owners, subcontractors, vendors, engineering firms, and design partners.
Establish project deadlines and continuously monitor progress to ensure work remains on schedule.
Drive a strong culture of safety when visiting project sites and ensure safety practices are consistently enforced.
Support the acquisition of new work by participating in marketing efforts, proposals, and presentations.
Provide leadership that fosters an environment of inclusion and diversity within project teams.
Assist in developing preconstruction packages, conducting project meetings, setting project milestones, and establishing project-specific schedules.
Establish and maintain subcontractor relations, approve pay applications, manage close-out processes, and ensure fair and professional treatment of all subcontractors.
Review contract documents, scopes of work, drawings, and specifications to confirm clarity and alignment with project objectives.
Organize and archive contract and project-specific documentation, including certified payrolls, daily reports, transmittals, submittals, submittal logs, issues lists, RFIs, RFI logs, material orders, material tracking logs, and invoices for accounts receivable and payable.
Adhere to company financial procedures, review and manage costs to date, and project costs to complete for accurate financial forecasting.
Enforce project safety plans and maintain clear communication with all related parties regarding specific safety requirements.
Maintain open and effective field and office communications, including regular site visits and consistent documentation in accordance with company policy.
Train and mentor Assistant Project Managers and other staff members to support their professional growth.
Demonstrate strong work ethic, self-motivation, and the ability to multi-task and solve problems while maintaining high levels of attention to detail and organization.
Exhibit strong presentation, verbal and written communication, problem-solving, financial, and leadership skills to support effective project delivery.
Maintain composure, professionalism, and objectivity in difficult situations and effectively resolve conflicts among stakeholders.
Develop and maintain positive working relationships with clients, the public, subcontractors, and suppliers.
Align personal performance with high standards of excellence, including being self-motivated, results-oriented, adaptable, team-oriented, accountable, and ethical.
Supervise Assistant Project Managers, Senior Project Engineers, Project Engineers, Superintendents, and Quality Control personnel to ensure cohesive project execution.
Communicate with staff and clients throughout the project, make informed decisions, and monitor progress to keep the project on schedule.
Collaborate with all levels of management and project team members to establish project needs, deadlines, and budgets, and to resolve conflicts to maintain a productive work environment.
Ensure reasonable accommodations are considered to enable individuals with disabilities to perform essential project functions.

Essential Skills

At least 5 years of Federal Project Manager experience, including direct management of projects valued at over $20 million.
Proven federal construction experience working for a general contractor.
Active Construction Quality Management (CQM) certification or relevant federal project management certifications that qualify the individual for site badging and approval.
Demonstrated experience in contract administration, change order management, procurement, scheduling, and financial reporting for construction projects.
Strong understanding of federal construction requirements, quality control processes, and project documentation standards.
Ability to lead and supervise Assistant Project Managers, Project Engineers, Superintendents, and Quality Control staff.
Strong work ethic with the ability to multi-task, remain self-motivated, and serve as a proactive problem-solver.
Excellent attention to detail and organizational skills to manage complex project documentation and workflows.
Demonstrated business acumen with strong presentation, verbal and written communication, and financial management skills.
Proven leadership ability, including the capacity to make timely and effective decisions and guide teams through challenges.
Ability to maintain composure, professionalism, and objectivity in difficult situations and effectively resolve conflicts.
Capability to develop and maintain positive working relationships with clients, subcontractors, suppliers, and other stakeholders.
Commitment to high standards of excellence, including being results-oriented, adaptable, team-focused, accountable, and ethical.
Knowledge of and ability to enforce construction safety plans, including relevant OSHA safety practices.
Experience working in federal environments as a Project Manager, Quality Control Manager (QCM), or Superintendent.

Additional Skills & Qualifications

Experience managing federal construction projects for a general contractor in roles such as Project Manager, Quality Control Manager, or Superintendent.
Familiarity with federal project requirements, quality control processes, and documentation standards.
OSHA 30-hour safety training or equivalent safety-related experience is highly beneficial.
Experience leading and mentoring Assistant Project Managers and other project staff.
Background in organizing and maintaining detailed project records, including RFIs, submittals, certified payrolls, and material tracking logs.
Ability to support business development activities by participating in marketing, proposals, and client presentations.
Demonstrated ability to foster an inclusive and diverse team environment.
Comfort working in both field and office settings, with the ability to travel to project sites as required.

Work Environment

This role operates primarily in an outdoor construction environment, where most work is conducted on active project sites exposed to the elements. The Project Manager should expect to work in hot, cold, rainy, or windy conditions, with appropriate clothing and safety gear provided to help mitigate environmental risks. The position regularly requires walking, climbing stairs, sitting, and standing for extended periods. Normal levels of talking and hearing are needed to communicate with team members and stakeholders. Visual demands include close vision, distance vision, color vision, peripheral vision, depth perception, and the ability to adjust focus. The role involves reaching with hands and arms and using hands and fingers to operate tools, equipment, and business machines. The Project Manager must be able to lift and move up to 50 pounds as needed in support of project activities. Construction projects often follow strict timelines, so after-hours work, including evenings and weekends, may be required to meet critical deadlines. Travel to various project locations is expected and may be frequent, reflecting the nature of a traveling, self-perform workforce built for rapid mobilization.

Job Type & Location

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Dumfries, VA.

Pay And Benefits

The pay range for this position is $35.00 - $60.00/hr.

Individual compensation offered for this position within this range will depend on many factors, including qualifications, skills, relevant experience, job knowledge, geographic location, internal equity, and other pertinent job-related factors.

Eligibility requirements apply to some benefits and may depend on your job classification and length of employment. Benefits are subject to change and may be subject to specific elections, plan, or program terms. If eligible, the benefits available for this temporary role may include the following: Medical, dental & vision Critical Illness, Accident, and Hospital 401(k) Retirement Plan Pre-tax and Roth post-tax contributions available Life Insurance (Voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependents) Short and long-term disability Health Spending Account (HSA) Transportation benefits Employee Assistance Program Time Off/Leave (PTO, Vacation or Sick Leave)

Job Type & Location

This is a Contract to Hire position based out of Dumfries, VA.

Application Deadline

This position is anticipated to close on Oct 29, 2026.

Workplace Type

This is a hybrid position in Dumfries,VA.

About KACE

KACE delivers technology-enabled mission services that advance public health, public safety, and national security, combining our large-scale operational capabilities with advanced technologies and data insights to meet the government’s most complex challenges.

At KACE, purpose and service are at the heart of everything we do, and every role plays a part in the mission. We’re proud to be certified as a Great Place to Work! This is an honor that reflects the voices of our employees and the culture we’ve built together. This certification recognizes our commitment to creating an inclusive, supportive, and engaging workplace where employees feel valued, heard, and empowered. At KACE, being a Great Place to Work means we prioritize professional growth, celebrate achievements, encourage collaboration, and foster an environment where innovation thrives.

The KACE Way is our commitment to our employees, to our customers, and to our communities. Join KACE and make a difference!

Job Summary

The National Targeting Center Intelligence/Targeting Analyst supports all Inspection Service criminal programs. This position will provide intelligence and targeting analyst support services in conjunction with Federal and State partners to the Inspections Service and other government agencies. The analyst must be capable of using technology solutions to actively search, collect, analyze, and prioritize information to identify high value targets and support high impact investigations in a fast-paced environment.

Essential Functions And Responsibilities

General knowledge of federal statutes.
Experience supporting narcotics investigations.
Financial analysis and understanding of financial regulatory processes.
Experience with Bank Secrecy (BSA) data and the Southwest Border Trac Record Analysis Center (SWB Trac).
Experience tracking money laundering and structuring activities of transnational criminal organizations.
Extensive experience in analyzing data and interpreting patterns or trends using appropriate analytical techniques and methods.
Proficiency conducting research on the internet and commercial as well as public databases.
Experience with mapping platforms such as ArcGIS.
Experience with phone toll analysis conducted using PLX or PenLink.
Experience using analytical tools and visualization software such as the i2 Analysts Notebook, Microstrategy, Tableau, and QLIK.
Experience working on time-sensitive projects, often under pressure with the ability to multi-task various tasks at the same time.
Foreign languages desirable, including Spanish.

Work Duties and Tasks

Include, But Are Not Limited To

Intelligence Gathering and Assessment

Evaluate information from a variety of sources to include agency databases, investigative resources, social media, chats, forums, dark net, Tor network, news feeds, internet relay chats, and other sources of data openly available on the Internet. Perform a prioritized assessment of the data to identify the most critical and reliable data in order to identify criminal activity monetization methods, locations, accounts, services, travels, email addresses, IP addresses, and other pattern of life data in an effort to determine attribution.

Data Analysis

Analyze data to identify and interpret patterns and trends, assess data quality, and eliminate irrelevant data; present findings in reports and presentations in non-technical terminology to various audiences.

Reporting Responsibilities

Responsible for documenting and reporting analytical results, creating graphic displays and reports that present clear and concise representations of the information analyzed; and disseminating data as required by the assigned task(s).

Preparatory Investigation

Assist Inspectors with developing intelligence for criminal investigations. Prepare initial investigative research for referral. Compile basic background information, USPIS sourced information, and intelligence from third-party entities such as commercial databases, law enforcement agencies, and victims.

Asset identification

Develop the required level of proof needed to seize and forfeit assets via civil, criminal, and administrative forfeiture processes; utilize compliance databases such as the USPS Bank Secrecy Act Database, SWB Trac and FINCEN to identify and locate assets. Assist with subpoena content creation, property/vehicle title & lien review and open-source searches of relevant financial data and asset ownership.

Minimum Qualifications & Skills

A Bachelors’ Degree from an accredited college or university in finance, information security, data science, intelligence, or other computer technology.
A minimum of (5) five years’ experience demonstrating the ability to review information, conduct analysis, conduct research, and communicate effectively orally and in writing. Experience supporting criminal investigations is highly desired.
Significant demonstrated experience will be considered in lieu of the education requirement.

Applicants selected may be subject to a government background investigation and may be required to meet the following conditions of employment.

Security Requirements/Background Investigation Requirements

Must be a U.S Citizen.
Favorable credit check for all cleared positions
Successfully passing a background investigation including drug screening.
Residency Requirement: Must have resided in the United States for the past five (5) years without residing outside of the United States for six (6) or more consecutive months during that period.

Fingering/Grasping/Feeling: Must be able to write, type, and use a telephone system 100% of the time.

Westat is a leader in research, data collection and analysis, technical assistance, evaluation, and communications. Our evidence-based findings help clients in government and the private sector accelerate advancements in health, education, transportation, and social and economic policy. Our dedication to improving lives through research and our approach to projects grounded in investigative curiosity, statistical and data rigor, adaptive methods, and advanced technology are why clients find exceptional value in our work.

Job Summary

Westat has an immediate opening for a Research Analyst to join our team of leading researchers supporting our continued work on behavioral health and health policy. You will be assisting with projects that address the needs of individuals with mental health conditions and substance use disorders.

In this highly collaborative role, you will work closely with project leadership and multi-disciplinary project teams to help translate science into resources for diverse audiences including federal and state policy makers, clinical service providers, and individuals affected by mental health conditions and substance use disorders. In this role, you will have substantive opportunities to assist with research on behavioral health topics such as behavioral health system transformation, healthcare financing, behavioral health program evaluations, mental health and substance use services, recovery and resilience, substance misuse prevention, overdose prevention, opioid and stimulant use disorders, and advancing access to effective behavioral health care.

We value regular in-person collaboration and preference will be given to candidates who can work 2 days per week at our Bethesda, Maryland office or at one of our other Westat office locations.

Job Responsibilities

Support all stages of research from study design through data collection and management, analysis, and report writing
Conduct literature searches, synthesize research findings, and contribute to writing on health policy and behavioral health topics
Assist in synthesizing research findings
Conduct data collection efforts, such as administering surveys, interviews, site visits, observation protocols, and acquiring administrative data
Provide technical assistance and training to federal grantees and other stakeholders

A master’s degree in public policy or a social science discipline, such as sociology, economics, political science, psychology or in analytical methods such as applied statistics; or a bachelor’s degree in public policy or a social science discipline, such as sociology, economics, political science, psychology or in analytical methods such as applied statistics and 2-5 years of relevant experience

Experience creating data visualizations based on evaluation data
US Citizenship is required by contract

Knowledge of public health approaches to evaluate mental health conditions and substance use disorders and service delivery
Experience using library databases to identify relevant journal articles and reports and reference management tools to organize sources
Experience with data collection, developing analysis plans, and overseeing analyses
Experience working on Federal government contracts, especially for the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA)
Demonstrated experience working on multiple projects quickly and simultaneously
Excellent written, verbal, and organizational skills

At Trident Systems Space Electronic Systems (SES) division, we believe in the power of using strong engineering principles to drive innovation and solve complex problems. We foster a culture of rigorous engineering and continuous improvement, leveraging the full knowledge of our organization through collaborative product development processes that include design and peer reviews. We combine our expertise in space electronics with right-sized development processes to create innovative, high-performance space-based electronic systems that meet our customers' evolving needs.

We are a mission partner supporting DoD, Intelligence Community, and Civil space customers. We develop complex, radiation effects mitigated, designs that balance competing requirements in modern space programs, delivering cutting-edge solutions that enable our customers to achieve more in space.

Position Summary

The Principal Engineering Technical Project Manager (TPM) will drive the execution and financial control of complex, integrated hardware and software engineering developments for aerospace and defense programs. Acting as both the primary operational steward and a leader for critical program control accounts, the TPM is directly accountable for cost and schedule execution.

The successful candidate will leverage an engineering background to deeply understand technical scope, coordinate cross-functional activities, and serve as the central execution leader for the development team. In this role, the TPM will proactively identify technical risks, track hardware/software integration dependencies, and partner with Program Management and functional leadership to resolve variances. Execution will require a strong command of both traditional Integrated Master Schedules (IMS) and Agile development methodologies.

Duties And Responsibilities

The Engineering Engineering Technical Project Manager (TPM) balances oversight with rigorous financial control to ensure engineering programs are delivered on time and within budget.

Budget Ownership: Manage cost accounts, monitor budgets, and take full accountability for cost and schedule compliance.
Variance Tracking: Analyze weekly cost and schedule variances, identify root causes, and implement corrective actions.
Forecasting: Maintain accurate Estimates at Completion (EAC) based on actual engineering progress and remaining work.
Schedule Optimization: Partner with schedulers to maintain a realistic, logic-driven Integrated Master Schedule (IMS).
Bridge Agile & Waterfall: Translate Agile engineering metrics (sprints, velocity) into traditional milestone tracking.
Resource Planning: Forecast engineering staffing needs to ensure the team can meet upcoming deliverables.
Ability to support travel or off-site work, as needed.
Perform other duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science/Engineering, Software Engineering, or a related technical discipline (or equivalent relevant experience).
Minimum of 9 years of professional engineering and development experience within the aerospace and defense industry.
Prior experience serving as a Technical Project Manager (TPM) or Cost Account Manager (CAM) or working intimately within an Earned Value Management System (EVMS) framework.
Technical Acumen: Solid understanding of the full hardware and software development lifecycle, hardware/software integration, and Agile methodologies.
Leadership & Communication: Strong interpersonal, communication, and leadership skills with a proven ability to collaborate effectively across cross-functional teams.

Preferred Qualifications

Experience leading multi-disciplinary engineering teams or serving as a technical lead/product owner.
Certified Scrum Master (CSM), SAFe Agilist/Scrum Master, or equivalent Agile certification.
Project Management Professional (PMP)

jobs.title: IT Project Manager
jobs.description:
While predominantly known for the role Cafcass takes in supporting almost 140,000+ children and young people in family court cases, what may be less well known is that our targeted use of technology is a key factor in ensuring we are at the forefront of our sector.

A digital organisation rated ‘outstanding’ by Ofsted in 2024, our IT team, in collaboration with our private sector partners, provides the technology that is a critical enabler for our diverse, flexible, mobile workforce. We are proud to work hand-in-hand with colleagues to provide the tools and services that ultimately benefit children and families.

Whilst technical expertise is important, what really sets us apart, and what we’re looking for each and every member of our team, is personal values and qualities that align with the important work Cafcass does.

About The Role

We are seeking an IT Project Manager to support the successful delivery of a portfolio of IT projects and programmes across Cafcass.

Working closely with the IT team, our partners and stakeholders from the wider business, you will lead the delivery of a number of IT projects, provide leadership to project teams, and ensure that agreed outcomes and benefits are delivered to time, cost and quality. Whilst we already achieve a 95% staff satisfaction with our technology, we have an ambitious programme in place to make it even better.

We would also like to invite you to register to meet some of our team and find out more about this role and working at Cafcass. If you would like to join this session that we’ll host on Teams, please click here.

We hope this will help you decide if this is an opportunity that interests you or not.

Key responsibilities

Lead and manage IT projects from initiation through to implementation.
Provide visible leadership to project teams.
Plan and manage multiple projects concurrently within agreed governance.
Select and apply appropriate delivery methodologies (e.g. Agile, Waterfall)
Manage project budgets, risks, issues and dependencies.
Ensure project benefits are clearly defined, tracked and realised.
Challenge assumptions and provide assurance on plans, delivery and outcomes.
Report progress, risks and finances to sponsor boards and senior leaders.
Build strong partnerships with business stakeholders, Project Management Office and suppliers.

About You

You will be a confident and experienced IT Project Manager with strong leadership capability and a track record of delivering change in demanding environments.

You Will Have

Substantial IT project management experience, including risk, issue and budget management.
Experience of leading project teams and working with external suppliers.
Distinctive blend of business, IT, financial and communication skills, because this is a highly visible position with substantial impact.
In depth theoretical and hands-on experience of project management methodologies e.g. agile, waterfall.
Excellent stakeholder engagement and communication skills.
Experience working with sensitive and confidential data.
A strong desire to have a positive impact on the support we offer Children and Families.

Desirable

Practitioner‑level project management qualification.
Degree‑level qualification (preferably IT‑related).

What we offer

In addition to a competitive salary, we offer generous annual leave (28 days rising to 33 days with 5 years’ continuous service, and it may be possible to recognise your current service), a Local Government Pension Scheme with significant employer contribution and a range of other financial and non-financial benefits to support your financial, physical and mental wellbeing.

Where you will work

If you join us, whilst your contractual office base will be one of the 30+ offices we have across England, it is highly likely you will work remotely as you will be part of a team based around the country. However, you can expect some level of national travel for things like meetings with your team, project stakeholders and key suppliers.

Timeline

Here Is An Indicative Timeline For The Recruitment Process

Meet the team and find out more

12th October 2026

Closing date

14th October 2026 *

Initial interview (remote via Teams)

21st to 23rd October

Final interview (in-person, Coventry)

3rd November

If you commence your application by no later than 18:00 on the closing date, you can then complete, review and submit your application until 23:59 the same day.

Whilst we hope to follow the above timeline and process, but both are subject to change if we deem it necessary. For example, the initial deadline isn’t too far away, but we reserve the right to extend. If we do, this doesn’t necessarily reflect the quality of anyone that has already applied, only that we wish to extend to allow more people to apply and give ourselves the broadest pool of applicants to consider.

While we don’t wish to discourage you from using AI as a support tool, applications should reflect your own thinking, experience and voice. An overreliance on AI‑generated content may limit our ability to assess your suitability and the values and qualities you may bring not only for the role, but also the organisation, so please take this opportunity to set out what is unique about you.

In anticipation of your application being successful, you might want to read about the offer and pre-employment checks process. As part of your application, you can highlight any concerns or questions about the pre-employment checks and we encourage all applicants to do so, safe in the knowledge such information will not be shared with individuals involved in the selection process.

Please be advised successful applicants will be subject to a range of pre-engagement checks, including a Disclosure and Barring Service check (DBS). In accordance with the DBS code of practice and our own policy, should an individual have a declared criminal offence an individual assessment will be completed. Further information on what the assessment covers can be found by viewing the Cafcass DBS policy.

We look forward to hearing from you.

Be Their Voice

We are Cafcass – the Children and Family Court Advisory and Support Service – and we represent children in family court cases in England.

Independently advising the family courts about what is safe for children and in their best interests, we speak up for over 130,0000 children every year when the family court makes critical decisions about their futures, ensuring their needs, wishes and feelings are heard.

Watch our video to find out we don’t just listen to children’s voices but we can be their voice.

If our purpose resonates with you, and you share our ambitions for children - exceptional experiences, for every child, everywhere and every time -
then if you join us, you will work alongside like-minded people in a diverse, inclusive and supportive organisation.

You will be trusted to work flexibly and independently using outstanding technology (e.g. touchscreen laptops, iPhone, all with first class support, including IT Trainers) with access to substantial resources (e.g. Cafcass Library has over 27,000 resources on social work, child protection and related topics). You will also have opportunities to develop, whatever team you join, wherever you are in the country and at whatever stage you are at in your career.

Whether you join us in one of our social work roles that work directly with children and families or our corporate and business services teams who provide technology, support and expertise, you will have the chance to make a difference for children and families. You can also find out more at www.cafcass.gov.uk/careers
.

Wellbeing

The wellbeing of our colleagues is something we are truly passionate about, as demonstrated by everyone having four dedicated, additional days per year when they are encouraged to spend time focusing on their health and wellbeing.

Colleagues can also have a health and wellbeing cash plan, for which Cafcass pays the basic premium (you can upgrade to include family members), which allows them to claim back some costs of routine health expenses, including dental check-ups, eye tests, physiotherapy sessions and more.

Overall, we foster a holistic approach to supporting our colleagues, benefitting physical, mental and financial health. This is led by a dedicated in-house team, the benefits of which include meaning support is targeted and specific to what colleagues need. Our team can also offer support and guidance when it comes to specific health conditions, such as neuro-diverse conditions, cancer and the menopause.

Our wellbeing offer is further strengthened by an external Employee Assistance Provider (EAP) which provides a free confidential support service 24 hours a day. This means access to clinical and professional expertise which gives you a chance to talk about all kinds of work and personal issues.

If this wasn’t enough, we are especially proud that over 125 colleagues have completed training and receive ongoing support to act as Health and Wellbeing Champions. Furthermore, we have nearly 100 people that have trained to be Mental Health Allies.

Diversity

We represent children and families from diverse backgrounds and having a diverse workforce helps us to fulfil this responsibility authentically.

It also helps us to grow, evolve and innovate, so we particularly welcome applications from individuals from diverse backgrounds as we strive to ensure our workforce reflects the diversity of the children and families we work with.

We are proud to be a disability confident leader, we invite you to join our team, we are committed to actively attract and recruit individuals with disabilities including “non-visible” disabilities and mental health conditions. Our inclusive and accessible recruitment process means we aim to accommodate reasonable adjustments as needed. This commitment highlights our dedication to employing, training, retaining, and developing the careers of our colleagues with disabilities.

Our Diversity Networks provide a safe space for colleagues with shared aspects of identity and lived experience – supported by allies across the organisation. The networks help ensure we provide an inclusive working environment and a service which promotes the diversity and uniqueness of children and families from all backgrounds.

For more information watch our video here
.

Our Current Networks Include

Ability Matters

Colleagues with disabilities and long-term health conditions.

Carers Network

Colleagues with additional caring responsibilities for someone close to them who has a disability or long-term health condition.

Faith Network

Colleagues who are part of, or have an interest in, religious or spiritual faith communities.

Kaleidoscope Network

Colleagues from Black Asian and Minority Ethnic backgrounds.

Mental Health Network

Colleagues who experience, or have an interest in, Mental Health issues.

Pride

Network

Colleagues who identify as Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual and Trans – LGBT+.

Neurodiversity Network

Colleagues who are neurodivergent, or support someone who is.

Together

‘Together with Children and Families’ (which we just call ‘Together’) is the name of our relationship-based practice framework. It applies to the work of every individual in Cafcass, from Social Workers to Leaders and includes our Corporate and Business Support teams.

It is at the heart of what we do and is made up of our values, how these values work in practice, the tools to use to incorporate these values in our work and the impact this will have on the children and families we serve.

This framework encourages us to be pro-active and to look for the strengths in ourselves and others. It also enables us to build positive relationships with our colleagues, our partners and most importantly, with the children and families with whom we work.

We look forward to telling helping you learn more about Together should you join us.

Benefits

We know i

WSP is seeking EHV EPC Project Manager (Power Delivery)- Remote
for our Power & Energy Program Management Office in Portland, OR.
The following locations will also be considered: Los Angeles, CA, San Francisco, CA, San Diego, CA, Seattle, WA, Boise, ID, Helena, MT and Phoenix, AZ.
In this position, you will be responsible for cradle-to-grave execution of high-voltage transmission EPC projects, from project development and design through construction, energization, and final closeout.

This Opportunity

About Odys

At Odys, we’re mobilizing power, with Hybrid Power Systems developed for aerospace and in-demand everywhere. It’s the kind of mission diversity that demands a fresh way of thinking.

We began with an early bet on hybrid, when the mobility industry was focused on batteries. We designed, tested, and validated our first 1 MW high-speed generator in 12 months. And then we pushed further, developing systems with greater power density in less time. Today, our Hybrid Power Systems offer outputs ranging from 20 kW
to 4 MW
, with applications in the air or on the ground.

One of those applications is Laila
, an unmanned drone designed for critical logistics and defense missions. With its 100 kW-class onboard Hybrid Power System, Laila can support medical cold-chain transport or serve as an aerial platform for counter-UAS measures.

The market interest has been overwhelming: Over 30
inbound requests from leading US and global manufacturers, and 14+ DoD
contracts
.

Our team comes from deep tech and aerospace, with backgrounds spanning drone and aircraft development, high-volume production, and electrified mobility.

We operate with urgency and ownership at every level. We validated high-speed generator technology faster than our peers, not because we skipped steps, but because we've been doing this long enough to know which ones matter most.

Creating the future

This is a hands-on role close to the hardware. You will also support capture and proposal activity as we grow the pipeline and help stand up the quality and program process a company at our stage needs to scale.

Maintain risk and opportunity registers with real mitigations, and escalate with a recommendation rather than a status

Communicate program health clearly and honestly to leadership, with the underlying data behind it

LAZ Parking is one of the largest operators in the growing multi-billion-dollar US parking industry. Founded in 1981, LAZ operates hundreds of thousands of parking spaces from offices nationwide. When it comes to parking, we are the experts!

Most importantly, LAZ is a PEOPLE FIRST company with a mission to "create opportunities for our employees and value for our clients." If you're looking to join a growing company led by passionate people committed to being the best, contact us today!

The Spirit of the Position

The Project Management Office (PMO) supports projects across every department at LAZ, including Operations, Finance, Technology, HR, Client Services, and newly acquired or partner businesses. The Project Manager leads cross-functional teams, coordinates internal and external partners, and keeps projects moving toward organizational goals.

The PMO works as both a project lead and a consulting partner. Depending on the project, this role may run a project end to end or help a department plan and run their own work using PMO tools and resources. The right person for this role will be able to adapt to the needs of the business or project in an agile way, always identifying and executing to add value and support.

Principal Duties

Planning and delivery

Build short- and long-term project plans with clear milestones, owners, and deadlines
Track progress against the plan and keep timelines and quality on track
Adjust schedules, scope, and targets as business needs, priorities, or funding change
Coordinate go-live readiness, including user acceptance testing (UAT), data validation, training, pilot rollouts, and handoff to operational owners
Close out projects by confirming ownership transfer, documenting lessons learned, and capturing project outcomes

Team and partner leadership

Lead cross-departmental teams, making roles, responsibilities, and goals clear for everyone involved

Our client is building and expanding data center network capacity at fleet scale. As the accountable program lead, you would take approved network designs and turn them into predictable delivery across many sites, from new builds and capacity expansions to retrofits, refreshes and decommissions.

This is a program leadership role first. You will not configure network equipment, and you will not own the design. You will own the plan, the sequence and the commitment, and you will be the person who stops a deployment from starting when the design, materials or site are not ready.

What you will do

Own a half-over-half execution roadmap across new builds, front-end fabric projects, technology modifications, retrofits and special initiatives
Run intake and readiness gates, and refuse to start work until the design package, bill of materials, method of procedure, site requirements and dependency map are complete
Own delivery from kickoff through material arrival, installation, provisioning, validation, operational handoff and closeout
Hold portfolio-level visibility of hardware demand, supply and need-by dates, and make allocation trade-offs between competing projects and regions
Keep a risk and dependency register with quantified schedule impact, and run change control for design, BOM, scope and schedule changes
Align engineering, supply chain, construction, logistics, site teams and vendors, without direct authority over any of them
Present portfolio health, material risk and decisions needed to senior leadership
Build automated reporting and dashboards from imperfect operational data, and turn lessons learned into reusable playbooks

What we are looking for

10+ years of technical program or portfolio management in network infrastructure, data centers, cloud infrastructure or telecommunications
Ownership of complex, multi-site deployment programs from intake through operational handoff
Working knowledge of data center network fabrics, including spine and leaf, top of rack, physical topology and redundancy, enough to question a design package and hold your own with engineers
Hands-on experience with BOMs, hardware demand planning, material allocation and supply-risk management
Proven ability to prioritise concurrent programs that share hardware, engineering and field resources
A track record of building metrics, dashboards and automation that remove manual reporting
Executive communication, with concise written updates and confident readouts

Who this is not for

If your background is software, application or server program management, this role will not suit you.
The same applies to construction project management with no network content, or to program management that stops at coordination and never touches hardware supply or readiness gating.
Telecom, carrier and data center network deployment backgrounds are very welcome.

Preferred

Data center network fabric delivery at hyperscale or across a large fleet
Front-end fabric deployments, lifecycle retrofits, hardware migrations or decommissions
Experience partnering with construction, facilities, supply chain, logistics and field engineering
AI-assisted workflow optimisation or program analytics
PMP, PgMP, or network, cloud or data center certification

Do you love working with diverse set of customers and engineers? Are you excited about bringing clarity and delivering through ambiguity? Do you want to deliver initiatives that make it easy for builders, security and compliance teams to drive better security outcomes? Are you keen on solving problems that no other company has solved?

The Vulnerability Management and Remediation Engineering team is building the next generation of mission critical security systems for protecting Amazon assets. Our innovations enable fast, efficient, and effective security across the globe to keep customer's data safe. Our customers are Amazon, internal stakeholders, and Amazon’s customers. Our technical program managers work directly with stakeholders, get close to customers' needs, and are empowered to take technical risks to help build the best-in-class software with respect to quality, usability, and scale.

We are looking for an experienced Senior Technical Program Manager who will support VMR Engineering teams to design and deliver security outcomes that positively impact our security posture at scale for Amazon customers and builders. Characteristics that will make this candidate effective include demonstrated abilities to: [1] dive deep into complex problem spaces while maintaining focus on the larger strategic objectives, [2] build trust and negotiate mutually beneficial outcomes with partners through transparency and delivery on commitments, and [3] communicate with clarity and candor to distill complex topics into simple terms while practicing respect for diverse ideas.

Key job responsibilities

You will partner with security and engineering leaders across Amazon business and security teams to work backwards from customer security outcomes, design initiatives to achieve those outcomes, and drive delivery against those commitments.
You will operate amidst ambiguity, where the problem and strategy may not be defined. You will deliver clarity by leading through your team and collaborating with partner teams to define the strategic vision, and influence program and product roadmaps and strategies that will realize that vision.

We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, training, and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional.

Work/Life Balance

We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve.
